I farm 15 mu, and I do not start from zero. I look at what worked around me last year and then I adjust a little. We have well water, so I will lean on wheat and maize for the main income, because that is the steady part on my land. Cotton can still make money, but it needs more watching and more sprays, so I will not put too much area into it since some people in my family work off-farm and labor is tight in busy time. I will keep 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and put 5 mu in cotton. For seed, I will use the kinds that neighbors planted well the last two years. I am willing to spend on fertilizer because losing yield hurts more than using a bit extra, but I still count the money carefully. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer and give water about three times with the well, because if wheat is short of water at jointing and filling, yield drops fast. For summer maize after wheat, time is short, so I will do no-tillage or very light direct seeding after harvest to save labor and catch moisture, then give two waters if rain is not enough. For cotton, I will use a better seed, give more potash than before, and spray more times because insects on cotton are troublesome here. I will keep the plan simple and close to what I know, not make big risky changes.
